Asset: WELL-0071 (SW-24 Well 071, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 30 Jun 2024 08:00 · Finished: 23 Jul 2024 03:00 · Well stopped for this job: 547 hours Crew lead: Daniel Foster (U-302) · Crew: Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0071-0088 on 2024-06-27 Report written: 24 Jul 2024

What happened

Field staff reported that the motor breaker kept tripping and the pump jack would not run. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0071-0088 showed the wellhead at 35.5 °C with the air at 35.0 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. An insulation test showed a winding fault, so the motor was replaced with an exchange unit. The well stayed shut in for about 21 days longer than the repair itself because heavy rain made the lease road impassable for the service truck.

Root cause

Moisture got into the motor terminal box and damaged the windings.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 2 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Disconnected and removed the motor.
  2. Fitted the exchange motor on the existing base.
  3. Aligned the sheaves and tensioned the belts.
  4. Checked rotation direction and motor current.

Summary of the fix: replaced the electric motor with an exchange unit.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours; motor current within the nameplate rating and stroke rate normal. The well was returned to production.

Asset: WELL-0071 (SW-24 Well 071, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: rod string Work started: 14 Jun 2025 08:00 · Finished: 24 Jun 2025 07:00 · Well stopped for this job: 239 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Brian Coleman Triggered by: inspection INS-0071-0136 on 2025-06-12 Report written: 25 Jun 2025

What happened

Field staff reported that the operator noticed the pump jack running unusually light and no fluid reaching the flowline. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0071-0136 showed the wellhead at 35.7 °C with the air at 29.7 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A dynamometer card showed no load from the downhole pump, which points to a parted rod. The company workover rig was busy on other wells, so the well waited about 8 days for it; the work itself took about 2 days.

A coupling unscrewed after repeated rod buckling at the bottom of the stroke.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0071-030

Asset: WELL-0071 (SW-24 Well 071, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: flowline Work started: 02 Jan 2026 08:00 · Finished: 02 Jan 2026 18:00 · Well stopped for this job: 10 hours Crew lead: Megan Ward (U-305) · Crew: Kevin Price, Brian Coleman · Contractor: Tumbleweed Flowline Co. Triggered by: inspection INS-0071-0164 on 2026-01-01 Report written: 02 Jan 2026

What happened

The weekly drone inspection INS-0071-0164 at 10:15 on 2026-01-01 found crude oil on the pad: about 7.2% of the pad area, estimated 4.0 bbl. The inspector noted: "Dark staining on pad." The field operator shut the well in, closed the flowline valve and placed earth berms and absorbent pads. The release was contained about 1.9 hours after the inspection. The crew traced the leak to a threaded coupling on the flowline close to the wellhead.

Root cause

Thread fatigue from pump jack vibration. This is corrective repair number 3 on this well's flowline in the last 12 months.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).

Work done

  1. Excavated around the coupling.

  5. Excavated the stained soil.
  6. Backfilled after the pressure test.

Maintenance Report — MNT-0071-032

Asset: WELL-0071 (SW-24 Well 071, T200, Southwest Block 24) Equipment: pump jack Work started: 27 Feb 2026 08:00 · Finished: 03 Mar 2026 20:00 · Well stopped for this job: 108 hours Crew lead: Brian Coleman (U-304) · Crew: Daniel Foster, Kevin Price · Contractor: Coyote Ridge Well Services Triggered by: inspection INS-0071-0172 on 2026-02-26 Report written: 03 Mar 2026

What happened

Field staff reported that the pump jack was running rough with a loud knock at the top of each stroke, so the operator stopped it. The thermal reading at inspection INS-0071-0172 showed the wellhead at 16.8 °C with the air at 12.6 °C, so the well was not producing. The operator shut the well in for the repair. A vibration check and visual inspection found play in the saddle bearing and scoring on the bearing housing. The well stayed shut in for about 2 days longer than the repair itself because the crew was committed to a higher-priority spill response elsewhere in the field.

Root cause

Bearing wear from long service and an overdue grease interval.

Safety and permits

  • Pre-job safety meeting held with the crew before work started (WS-01).
  • Energy isolated: prime mover stopped at the bottom of the stroke, brake set and chained, motor disconnect locked and tagged, wellhead wing valve closed and tagged, pressure bled off (WS-02).
  • Personal H2S monitors worn; highest reading 0 ppm, below the 10 ppm stop-work level (WS-03).

Work done

  1. Lowered the horsehead and supported the walking beam with a crane.
  2. Removed the saddle bearing assembly.
  3. Cleaned the housing and checked alignment.
  4. Fitted a new saddle bearing and torqued the bolts to the manufacturer's values.
  5. Greased all structural bearings.

Summary of the fix: replaced saddle bearing and re-greased.

Testing and return to service

Ran the unit for 2 hours: smooth stroke, no knocking, bearing temperature normal. The well was returned to production.
